title: AppSettings
description: The app settings document shared by the desktop, LAN, and headless hosts.

custom_tools.description: Accepted custom executables, re-probed when the service starts.

default_project_template_id.description:
The template a new project copies. `null` means no template is marked default, so a
new project starts on the engine defaults.

delete_chunks_on_success.description: Whether encoded chunks are deleted after a successful run.

encoder_forks.description:
Saved encoder forks: a named build of a known encoder, with its own executable and
parameter descriptors. A fork is an extra catalogue entry; it never replaces the
provider another screen chooses.

encoder_overrides.description:
User edits to the engine's built-in descriptors, keyed by encoder id. A fork keeps
its own parameter map on the fork instead.

project_templates.description:
Every saved project template, in name order. A template is a complete configuration
plus a General section; a project copies one at creation and then owns its copy.

python_interpreter.description:
The Python interpreter the script editor's language server analyses, or `null` to
use the one the host resolves: an activated `VIRTUAL_ENV` or `CONDA_PREFIX`, then
`python` on `PATH`, then the Windows launcher's installs, then the staged bundled
runtime. Packages belong to an interpreter, so a venv is invisible to the server
until this points at it; one interpreter serves every script, which makes it a
machine setting rather than project configuration.

reduce_motion.description:
Reduce motion even when the operating system does not ask for it. `false` follows
the OS preference, which is never overridden.

scene_model.description:
The TransNetV2 ONNX model this machine uses, or `null` to let the engine search its
standard locations. One file serves every project, so this is an application
setting rather than project configuration.

temp_dir.description: Temporary-directory override; `null` uses the app-data default.

tool_sources.description:
The source each capability uses: `bundled` or `system`. An absent key is automatic,
which selects the bundle when it is present and healthy and the machine's install
otherwise. VapourSynth is one compound id because its runtime, Python, and plugins
must come from the same bundle.

Choice.description: One value of a choice parameter.

description.description: Optional explanation shown beside the label.

ChoicePresentation.description: How a choice parameter's options are drawn.

oneOf.description: Radio or segmented up to four options, a dropdown above that.
Radio buttons.
Segmented control.
Dropdown list.

max_selected.description: Most selections accepted, when there is a limit.

multiple.description: Whether more than one option may be selected.

options.description: Every accepted value, with the label the user reads.

value_kind.description:
Declared value type; absent on descriptors authored before the distinction,
where the options themselves decide.

ChoiceValueKind.description:
The value type a choice parameter's options carry.

A choice is not always text: an encoder that spells a mode as `0`, `1`, `2` still
wants "Main", "High", "Professional" in the editor, and the editor must know that
the value it stores is a number rather than the label it draws.

oneOf.description: Options are text values.
Options are numeric values with human labels.

CollectionItemKind.description: The value type of one collection item.

oneOf.description: A number item.
A text item.
A choice item.
A path item.
A duration item.

CollectionPresentation.description: How a collection parameter's items are drawn.

oneOf.description: Removable chips.
Values typed into one comma-separated field.

item.description:
The kind of every item. A flag or a nested collection is not a value, so the item
kind excludes both; that also keeps the schema acyclic.

max_items.description: Most items accepted, when there is a limit.

separator.description: Separator used to encode the list into one argument.

CustomTool.description: One accepted custom executable saved in app settings.

kind.description:
Executable family, keyed by the engine encoder: `aom`, `svt-av1`, `rav1e`, `vpx`,
`avm`, `x264`, `x265`, `vvenc`, or `ffmpeg` for muxing.

Delimiter.description: How a parameter's key and value are joined into argv entries.

oneOf.description: Two argv entries: the key and the value are separate.
One argv entry: `--crf=22`.

max.description: Largest accepted value, when one is known.

min.description: Smallest accepted value, when one is known.

unit.description: Unit the value is expressed in.

DurationUnit.description: The unit a duration parameter is expressed in.

oneOf.description: Whole seconds.
Milliseconds.
Frame count.

EncoderFork.description:
A saved build of a known encoder, with the parameters its own `--help` reports.

A fork is a catalogue entry, not a provider replacement: the user may keep SVT-AV1 on
`PATH` as the default and still add one or more custom SVT-AV1 builds. Selecting a fork
in a project writes its executable path into that project's engine encoder document, so
the engine runs exactly the binary the user chose.

base.description:
The engine encoder this build of: `aom`, `svt-av1`, `rav1e`, `vpx`, `avm`, `x264`,
`x265`, or `vvenc`.

id.description: Stable user-chosen slug, unique within the catalogue.

label.description: Human-readable name shown in the encoder list.

parameters.description:
Parameter descriptors parsed from `--help` or added by hand, keyed by canonical
spelling. These become the initial options when the fork is selected.

parameters_edited.description:
Whether the user changed the parameter map after it was saved. A service restart
re-probes an executable to refresh the map it parsed, but never replaces an edited
one; saving a path or clearing the flag is what asks for a fresh probe.

profile.description:
The shipped fork profile this build matched, if any. A known-fork row always names
its profile; a user-added build naming one gets that profile's table.

version.description: Version line observed by the probe, when it answered.

warning.description:
A non-fatal probe finding, such as a known-fork row whose executable did not show
the profile's signature. The row still uses the shipped table.

EncoderParameterOverride.description:
User edits to one built-in encoder's descriptors.

The map is the complete set the user wants to see, and `removed` records the engine keys
that map no longer contains. Keeping both means an engine parameter added in a later
build still appears unless the user hid it, and a descriptor the user added survives a
restart.

parameters.description: Descriptors the user added or replaced, keyed by canonical CLI spelling.

removed.description: Engine descriptors the user removed from the editor.

GeneralDefaults.description:
Project-level defaults applied to videos added from now on.

Existing queue entries keep the input and output they were created with. The defaults are
stored on the project rather than inferred at add time, so the LAN browser and the desktop
window add the same video from the same document.

ffms2_filters.description:
Native FFMS2 filters, kept as the engine's own typed JSON so the contract never
mirrors an enum that changes with the engine revision.

import_method.description:
Source plugin for the two VapourSynth input kinds. `None` means BestSource, the
engine's default, so a project written before this field existed keeps its decode
path.

index_file.description:
Optional `.ffindex` path for the native FFMS2 input. `None` lets the engine place the
index beside the source, which is what a machine without a prepared index expects.

input_kind.description: Decode path for a newly added source.

output_folder.description: Absolute folder used when `output_mode` is `folder`; absent otherwise.

output_mode.description: Where a newly added video's output path is derived.

script.description:
Absolute path to the `.vpy` file when `input_kind` is `vapour_synth_script` and
`script_mode` is `file`.

script_mode.description:
How the script input is supplied. A document written before this field existed has
`script` set and no mode, which is read as `file`.

vapour_synth_filters.description: VapourSynth filters, in the same engine-owned JSON form.

variables.description:
Extra variables the script reads as `condor_<name>`.

The runner injects its own reserved keys into the same map and replaces them on every
open, so a document cannot change what the scene table, the paths, or the sequence
configuration say.

InputKind.description: How the project decodes the sources of videos added to its queue.

oneOf.description: Native FFMS2 decode; requires no optional dependency.
VapourSynth decode through the project's selected import method.
A VapourSynth script file the engine loads and feeds its scene variables to.

Mark.description: One labelled position on a slider.

integer.description: Whether the value must be an integer.

max.description: Largest accepted value, when one is known.

min.description: Smallest accepted value, when one is known.

unit.description: Unit shown beside the value, for example `kbps`.

OutputMode.description: Where the output of a newly added video is written.

oneOf.description: Beside the source file, named after it.
Into one folder, named after the source file.

ParameterDescriptor.description: One encoder parameter, derived from the engine's CLI parameter or authored by the user.

advanced.description: Whether the field belongs behind the advanced disclosure.

default.description:
Suggested initial value for a user who enables the parameter. It is not applied until
the user sets the parameter.

delimiter.description:
`Some(Space)` emits two argv entries, `Some(Joined(..))` emits one, and `None` is a
boolean flag with no value.

group.description: Grouping shown in the parameter editor, for example `Quality`.

kind.description: The value type and all of its constraints.

relations.description: Validity rules involving another parameter in the same definition.

ParameterKey.description:
The identity of one encoder parameter, as it is written on the command line.

Prefix is part of the identity: `--crf` and `-crf` are different spellings even when
both reach the same encoder. JSON object keys are strings, so the value serialises as the
canonical `"{prefix}{name}"` form and deserialises from that same string.

ParameterKind.description:
The value type and all of its constraints for one parameter.

The kind is closed so an ill-typed constraint cannot be built. A `Flag` is a parameter
the engine emits when true and omits when false; a boolean spelled `0`/`1` by the CLI is
a two-value `Choice`, not a `Flag`.

oneOf.description: Boolean flag with no value.
A number, optionally bounded.
Text, optionally with a maximum length and a pattern.
One or more values from a fixed set.
A file or directory path.
A duration in the unit the encoder expects.
A list encoded into one delimited string.

ParameterRelation.description:
A validity rule that involves another parameter in the same definition.

A closed set rather than an expression language: Rust gets exhaustiveness and the
generated TypeScript gets a discriminated union. Only *set* parameters participate.

oneOf.description: This parameter is only valid when `other` is set to `equals`.

message.description: Message shown when the rule fails.

other.description: The parameter this one depends on.

oneOf.description: At least one of `others` must be set.

message.description: Message shown when the rule fails.

others.description: The parameters any one of which satisfies the rule.

oneOf.description: This number must be at least the value of `other`.

message.description: Message shown when the rule fails.

other.description: The parameter this one is compared with.

oneOf.description: This number must be at most the value of `other`.

message.description: Message shown when the rule fails.

other.description: The parameter this one is compared with.

oneOf.description: This parameter and `other` may not both be set.

message.description: Message shown when the rule fails.

oneOf.description: This parameter and `other` must carry the same value when both are set.

message.description: Message shown when the rule fails.

other.description: The parameter whose value must match.

ParameterValue.description:
A value a parameter can carry.

It is untagged on the wire, so a choice is written as the literal `0`, `"2"`, or `true`
rather than a wrapper object. The enum exists so generated TypeScript and Zod describe
exactly these variants instead of `unknown`.

anyOf.description: An explicit null, for a parameter whose unset state is meaningful.
A number; integers are not a separate variant.

A flat list of scalars, for a collection parameter. Nested lists are not a value a
CLI parameter can carry, so the recursion stops here.

accept.description: Suggested file extensions, without the leading dot.

directory.description: Whether the path must be a directory.

ProjectTemplate.description:
One named project template.

The configuration is materialised when the template is saved, so applying it needs no
engine default at read time and a later engine revision cannot change what a saved
template means. A project copies both documents and never references the template.

config.description: The complete engine configuration a project copies.

general.description: The General defaults a project copies.

id.description: Stable identifier; generated by the service, never reused.

name.description: Display name, unique case-insensitively among templates.

updated_at.description: Last write, in UTC ISO-8601 form.

ScriptInputMode.description: How a `vapour_synth_script` input supplies its script.

oneOf.description: A `.vpy` file on disk, used as written.
Script text stored in the project document.

TextFormat.description:
The well-known shape of a text value, when the encoder states one.

A format is evidence from the help text, not a guess: the editor validates the value and
the service still stores exactly what the encoder accepts.

oneOf.description: An email address.
An absolute or relative URL.
An ISO-8601 date or date-time.

format.description: A well-known value shape the editor validates, when the encoder states one.

multiline.description: Whether the editor should offer a multi-line field.

pattern.description: Regular expression the whole value must match.

VapourSynthImporter.description: The VapourSynth source plugin that imports a video into the decode graph.

oneOf.description: FFmpegSource, which needs no index file of its own.
BestSource, the engine's default and the fastest of the four for most sources.
L-SMASH-Works.
DGDecodeNV, which needs the `dgindexnv` executable.

Widget.description:
How a parameter's value is presented, independently of its type and constraints.

A range does not determine a control: CRF is best edited with a slider because its useful
range is small, while an unbounded frame count needs a plain input. `Auto` lets the
renderer apply the documented rules.

oneOf.description: Let the renderer choose from the kind and its constraints.
A slider with optional marks.
A plain numeric field.
One control for single- and multi-select; cardinality lives in `ChoiceSpec`.
A text field, optionally multi-line.

placeholder.description: Placeholder shown while the field is empty.

oneOf.description: A boolean flag; the parameter is emitted when true and omitted when false.

A two-state switch for a number whose only meaningful values are `0` and `1`.

Unlike `Toggle`, the parameter carries a value, so the switch writes `1` or `0` and
only clearing the option returns the encoder to its own default.
A file or directory picker.
A duration field with its unit.
A collection editor.
